_comment: Settings for the dice-skit audio pipeline.
Keys starting with _ are comments and are ignored.
Delete any setting to use its built-in default.
Command-line flags (strict=0, dry_run=1, loudness=0) override this file for one run.
Paths are relative to this file's folder.
_version: File format version. Do not edit.

_strict: What to do when a line's audio is missing, corrupt or unconvertible.
true: abort and leave the old master untouched. Use for the final build.
false: skip those lines and build the rest. Use while recordings are arriving.
The four mandatory checks abort either way and cannot be switched off.
_backend: auto: FFmpeg if installed, else the built-in joiner (recommended).
ffmpeg: always FFmpeg; fails if it is not installed.
python: built-in joiner; no FFmpeg needed, MP3 only.
run._batch_size: null = one pass (recommended). A number, e.g. 40, only if one pass runs out of memory.

_comment: Where files are read from and written to (doc section 14).
input, in_out and output are the three top-level folders; each may be relative to the project folder or absolute, e.g. D:/dice-skit-output.
The other folders are relative to their parent: csv and human_gen to input, machine_gen to in_out, master_dir, work and log to output.
output must not be inside input or in_out, nor contain them: 'stitch_mp3.py clean' deletes inside output.
paths._input: Top-level input folder. Never written by the pipeline except by fetch_drive.py, which downloads into human_gen.
paths._in_out: Top-level folder for material one stage writes and another reads: machine_gen.
paths._output: Top-level output folder: master, work and log. Everything in it can be rebuilt.
paths._csv: The script, inside input: lines, order, fillers, background scores.
paths._human_gen: Recorded takes and named sound files, inside input.
paths._machine_gen: TTS-generated takes, inside in_out. generate_mp3.py writes here; stitch_mp3.py reads it.
paths._master_dir: Folder for the finished master, inside output.
paths._work: Caches and generated silence, inside output. Safe to delete; rebuilt on the next run.
paths._log: One log file per run, inside output. 'clean' never deletes it.
paths._search_order: When both folders hold a file for the same take, the first listed wins.

output._comment: Format of the master and of every piece in it.
_sample_rate: Hz. 24000 matches the TTS output, so those files need no conversion (recommended for speech).
44100 or 48000 suit music-heavy productions, but every TTS line must then be converted.
_bitrate: Bits per second. Higher means better quality and a bigger file.
output._mono: true: right for dialogue. false: stereo, only if stereo music width matters; about twice the size.

fillers._comment: Generated silence between lines, always in the output format above.
_short_seconds: Gap before each line whose filler_before cell is empty.
Applies to almost every line: +1 s on 154 lines adds about 2.5 minutes.
fillers._long_seconds: Length of long_filler.mp3, for rows that name it, e.g. a scene change.

background_score._comment: Music under a line (doc section 10). Only affects rows with background_score and score_cues filled in.
background_score._duck_db: How far the faded track is turned down, below 0. -6 subtle, -14 faint but audible (default), -20 almost silent.
background_score._ramp_seconds: Crossfade length. 0.1 quick, 0.3 smooth (default), 1.0 slow. Keep it shorter than your shortest cue segment.
background_score._match_loudness: true: bring the music to the line's loudness before mixing (recommended). false: only if the music is pre-mastered to sit under dialogue.
background_score._limit: Peak ceiling for the mix, 0.5-1.0 of full scale. Lower only if mixes sound distorted.

loudness._comment: Even out volume across lines (doc section 11). Dialogue only; fillers, sound effects and music keep their levels.
loudness._enabled: false leaves each line at its recorded level; useful for comparing. Same as loudness=0 on the command line.
_target_lufs: -16 loud: phone speakers, noisy places; more lines get limited.
-19 balanced for speech (default). -23 broadcast standard; quieter, very little limiting.
loudness._true_peak_dbfs: Highest allowed peak. -1 default; -2 if the master will be re-encoded later, e.g. by an upload platform.

tts._comment: Generating lines with Sarvam (generate_mp3.py). The API key is never stored in this file.
tts._enabled: true generates missing lines and uses API credit.
tts._api_key_source: env: SARVAM_API_KEY from .env (today). keyring: Windows Credential Manager (recommended once a GUI exists).
tts._language: Language and accent, e.g. en-IN (Indian English), hi-IN (Hindi). See Sarvam's documentation.
tts._pace: Speaking speed. 1.0 normal; lower is slower. See Sarvam's documentation for the range.
tts._sample_rate: Rate requested from TTS. Keep it equal to output.sample_rate so generated lines need no conversion.
tts._overwrite_existing: true regenerates every line, e.g. after changing voice or pace. Uses API credit.

drive._folder_url: Shared Google Drive folder link. null means pass it on the command line.
drive._use_cookies: true only if the folder is not link-shared and needs your browser login.
